clue.text: One taken in by club cut-off bid meaning the opposite

indicators.note: something taken in by another is received inside it, so the numeral goes within the other letters

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: cut off means the word for a bid loses its final letter

parts.note: a call is a bid in bridge
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A bridge player makes a truncated bid that says the reverse of what is intended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like part of the surface's bridge player; it is the Roman numeral, and 'taken in by' places it inside the club-plus-bid run, just after the club.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony says one thing while intending its contrary, so an ironical remark carries the reverse sense.

clue.text: Roly-poly boy is a bit of a debauchee

indicators.note: the boy forms a part within the debauchee, so his letters go inside

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute rake
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A plump lad is something of a rake.
explanation.definitionFit: A roly-poly is a rolled suet pudding; a roulade is likewise something rolled up with a filling.

clue.text: Organ bellows-mender's instrument

parts.note: the nose is an organ of the body
Francis Flute is the bellows-mender in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: An organ belonging to the man who repairs bellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' and 'bellows' suggest a church organ; the organ is the nose and the bellows-mender is a character from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose flute is a pipe blown through the nostrils, played in Polynesia and elsewhere.

clue.text: Nice as pie, this cheese maker

indicators.note: pie is printer's jumbled type, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: This cheesemaker is very pleasant indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' (printers' pie, a jumble of type) rearranges NICE AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Casein is the main milk protein, which curdles and forms the curd from which cheese is made.

clue.text: County takes wickets in London.

parts.note: Leicestershire, an English Midlands county, is also called Leicester
in cricket the square is the central area where the wickets are pitched

explanation.surface: A county cricket side takes wickets in a match in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicestershire is an English county; in cricket the 'square' is the strip of ground where wickets are laid.
explanation.definitionFit: The square is a well-known public space in London's West End.

clue.text: Pliable journalist dragged his feet

parts.note: limp means floppy, easily bent
ED is the usual short form of editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A floppy reporter shuffled along reluctantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking lamely, scuffing along with a halting gait, is what dragging one's feet describes literally.

clue.text: 15 for someone on the rocks?

parts.note: taken with the answer to 15 down, this is a thing that recovers a shipwrecked person

explanation.surface: A gun dog for a person stranded or in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' suggests marital or money trouble or a drink; here it is a shipwrecked person, hauled in by a rescue rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope thrown to someone in danger saves them, and figuratively any rescue in a crisis.

clue.text: Extravagant chairman needs employment

parts.note: a professor holds a chair, and PROF is the short form
use means employment

explanation.surface: A lavish chairman needs work.
explanation.definitionFit: Profuse means abundant, lavish, given in great quantity.

clue.text: Scattering a girl's pearls all over the place

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name; with the possessive, DI'S

indicators.note: the word pearls is scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's pearl necklace is strewn everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges PEARLS to PERSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersal is the spreading out or scattering of things widely.

clue.text: Contracts for bags of money

definitions.meaning: as a verb: draws together, as one does the lips

explanation.surface: Agreements are being made to supply moneybags.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb of puckering the lips; the other is the noun for coin pouches or prize funds.

clue.text: The Chief Justice was rich, quiet, and —" (Macaulay)

definitions.text: The Chief Justice was rich, quiet, and —" (Macaulay)

parts.words: The Chief Justice was rich, quiet, and —" (Macaulay)
parts.note: a quotation from the historian Macaulay with its final word missing; the solver supplies the adjective of ill repute that ends the line

explanation.surface: A line from Macaulay's History describing a notorious judge, with its last word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaulay wrote of a Chief Justice that he 'was rich, quiet, and infamous'; the clue is a fill-in-the-blank quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means notorious, known widely for bad deeds, which completes Macaulay's damning description of the judge.

clue.text: Fellow in tea house in the Orient gets stimulant

indicators.note: the abbreviation for fellow goes inside the word for a tea house

parts.note: a cafe is a place serving tea and light meals
taken as written
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A man sitting in an oriental tea house is given a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The alkaloid in coffee and tea acts as a stimulant on the nervous system.

clue.text: In general, stick to peas or beans

indicators.note: the word for stick goes inside the name of the general

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
gum is to stick, as with glue

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, keep to pulses.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas and beans are the seeds of pod-bearing plants, the family botanists name for that kind of vegetable.

clue.text: Repeat broadcast about conduct

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to run a business is to conduct it

explanation.surface: A programme is aired again on the subject of behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun is a second showing of a programme already aired, as on television.

clue.text: Biblical advice to the sluggard in retrospect

definitions.meaning: Proverbs 6:6: go to the ant, thou sluggard, consider her ways; consider is regard
looking backwards, a heraldic term for a beast facing over its shoulder

explanation.surface: Looking back on the Bible's counsel to the lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, REGARD ANT is the Proverbs instruction to consider the ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic beast looking behind it is so described; the split form echoes the proverb about considering the industrious insect.

clue.text: The place for the Open University?

definitions.text: The place for the Open University?

parts.words: The place for the Open University?
parts.note: read not as the distance-learning institution but as a town hosting both golf's Open Championship and an ancient university

explanation.surface: Where is the Open University based?
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is a British distance-learning body; here 'Open' is golf's Open Championship, often held at this Scottish town with its old university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish town is home to golf's famous Old Course, a frequent Open venue, and to Scotland's oldest university.

clue.text: He recovers possession and gets game

definitions.meaning: one who gets back something lost
a gun dog that fetches shot birds

explanation.surface: A man wins the ball back and joins the game.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fetches back; a gun dog breed bred to bring shot birds to the hunter.

clue.text: Jewish formalist undone by Eastern harpies

indicators.note: undone means the word harpies is pulled apart and remade

explanation.surface: A strict religious observer brought low by eastern harpies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were an ancient Jewish sect noted for strict observance of the law, hence a formalist.

clue.text: Novice gets wind instrument on part of the course

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: the green is the putting area of a golf course
a horn is a brass wind instrument

explanation.surface: A beginner takes a trumpet-like instrument out onto the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is an inexperienced newcomer, a raw beginner.

clue.text: Intoxicating drink served in breakfast cup?

definitions.text: Intoxicating drink served in breakfast cup?

parts.words: Intoxicating drink served in breakfast cup?
parts.note: a boozy drink whose name suggests the thing served in a breakfast cup, the boiled one in its holder

explanation.surface: A strong drink poured into a breakfast cup.
explanation.walkthrough: A breakfast 'cup' suggests an egg cup; the drink is made with beaten egg and liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-flip, or eggnog, is hot beer or spirits beaten with egg and sugar.

clue.text: Appropriate to move silently

definitions.meaning: as a verb: take for oneself without right

explanation.surface: It is fitting to go about quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is pilfering, taking what is not one's own; the other is creeping by unnoticed.

clue.text: Absence of mind clearly not suffered by Proust

definitions.meaning: Proust wrote the vast Remembrance of Things Past, so he plainly had no memory loss

explanation.surface: Proust was evidently never absent-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcel Proust's great novel is a feat of recollection.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory, which Proust, whose great novel is all recollection, evidently did not have.

clue.text: Seating for the tourist class on a Jumbo?

definitions.text: Seating for the tourist class on a Jumbo?

parts.words: Seating for the tourist class on a Jumbo?
parts.note: sounds like economy seats on a jumbo jet, but the jumbo is an elephant carrying sightseers

explanation.surface: Economy seats on a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests a jumbo jet; it is an elephant, and the seat is the canopied one on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is a seat, often canopied, carried on an elephant's back for riders.

clue.text: Game played with two packs

parts.note: sounds like a card game using two decks, but the packs are the scrums of forwards in a football code

explanation.surface: A card game needing a double deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packs' suggests decks of cards; in rugby each team's forwards form a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British name for rugby union, played by two teams whose forwards form opposing packs.

clue.text: When it's on the news, it shows how quick people are

definitions.text: When it's on the news, it shows how quick people are

parts.words: When it's on the news, it shows how quick people are
parts.note: news is intelligence; put that word before this one and the phrase names the measure of quick-wittedness

explanation.surface: A broadcast item reveals how fast people react.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' means intelligence; with that word placed before it, the answer gives the IQ, a gauge of how quick-witted people are.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligence quotient is the score used to rate mental sharpness, so the word completes that phrase.

clue.text: Late alas, drunk, and completely at a loss

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the two words stagger into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Sadly, a tipsy latecomer is utterly confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the eight letters of LATE ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bewildered, as lost as a sailor far out on the ocean.

clue.text: Strip clubs (West End)

parts.note: dives are seedy clubs or bars

indicators.note: the end of the word West gives its final letter

explanation.surface: A striptease in the nightclubs of London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre and nightlife district; here 'End' just takes the last letter of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip off, to take away clothing or possessions.

clue.text: Gratuity, say, will suffice for a drink

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity

indicators.note: say tells the solver to speak the next word, so its sound is what is entered

parts.note: will contracts to 'll, which spoken after a tip is the same sound as the ending written here

explanation.surface: A small tip will be enough to buy a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'tip'll' sounds just like the answer; 'suffice for' is surface padding about a tip paying for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is a person's favourite alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Some hate the really refined

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people truly detest the posh.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and airy, too fine or light for this world.
